newsitem.title: USA: Aluminum offtake in autos to grow - Alumax.
newsitem.headline: Aluminum offtake in autos to grow - Alumax.

text.p: The use of aluminum in cars is set to rise strongly over the coming years, especially in Europe where consumption in this sector is much lower than in the U.S., Allen Born, Chief Executive of Alumax Inc.

"In the next century, I predict aluminum usage in the automotive sector growing at a clip of 10 percent annually," Born told delegates at the Alumitech meeting here, organised by the U.S. Aluminum Association.
U.S. vehicles today contain about 250 pounds of aluminum, and Born saw this amount rising to well over 300 pounds by the year 2000.
Much of this growth will come in engine castings, wheels, body panels and structural components, Born said.
"We will see huge growth in airbag housings, bumpers, brake parts, seat frames and air conditioning assemblies," Born said.
There was greater potential for aluminum in the European market where vehicles currently contain about 160 pounds, well below the U.S. level, Born said.
The building and construction markets in Asia and Latin America could also provide outstanding growth opportunities for aluminum, especially in China, Born said.
China's aluminum consumption in 1995 was 1.7 million tonnes, double 1990 consumption.
Even chewing gum was a runaway market in China and there was an obvious market for foil wrappers, Born said.
"We are planning to introduce domestically produced curtain wall to the (Chinese) market," Born said.
